Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the middle session! The players stride out to the middle. Kraigg Brathwaite and John Campbell are the openers for West Indies. Chris Woakes to start with the ball. Let's go...
... DAY 5, SESSION 2 ...

ENGLAND HAVE DECLARED! As expected! They have given themselves two sessions weather permitting to take the 10 wickets, whereas Windies will have to chase down 282 to win. Will they go for it? Don’t see that happening.

If we resume on time after break, England would have probably declared and it will/should be Windies batting. A good second session awaits. The post-Lunch session should start at 10.53 pm IST (5.23 pm GMT) unless the raingods have some other plans.

And we assume we won’t be seeing England bat again in this game after the break! They lead by 281 and that should probably be enough. They came out all guns blazing and all the batters went after the bowlers right from the word go. A few played some handy cameos to take the lead up to 19 short of 300.
Update - 10.13 pm IST (4.43 pm GMT) - The rain Is back! The covers are coming and that should be Lunch!

We are all set for Day 5 action! Kraigg Brathwaite leads his troops in the middle. Alex Lees and Zak Crawley stride out to the middle as well. Spin to begin with. Veerasammy Permaul to start the proceedings. Here we go...
PITCH REPORT - Sir Curtly Ambrose reckons that it's a very dry surface. There will be variable bounce from time to time and he expects the pitch to play the same way.

Jonny Bairstow is up for a chat. He says that the attitiude that the guys showed was great. Mentions that they need to dig deep again if they have to force a result today. Tells that the further they go, there's more pressure to accelerate or for them to bat out for a draw. Informs that some balls have kept low, the way Jack Leach bowled, he was unlucky. Tells that when they come to bowl today, it'll be interesting. Informs that they will bat normally in the first half an hour.

Veerasammy Permaul is up for a chat. He says that it's not a wicket where you can go and blast as a batsman, you need to be patient. Mentions that the faster you bowl, it becomes easier. Tells that one got to bowl slower. States that in T20 cricket, he has opened with the white ball so it's not a new role for him to open with the red cherry as well.

Windies on the other hand, need wickets and in a heap. That is the only slender hope they have of a win. We have seen this England batting fall apart before and the hosts will hope it is one of those days. The first session will probably give us an idea as to which way is this game heading to.

Hello and welcome to the coverage of the last day of the second Test between Windies and England. The draw seems the most likeliest result as of now but we have seen funny things in happen in cricket and something tells me, we could be in for a surprise here. England probably are the side with a bigger chance of a win if there’s a result. They’ll though need to score quickly int he first session, we may also see Root make a brave declaration to force a result. He would want his bowlers to get at least 2 sessions to take 10 Windies wickets. It will be interesting to see if the wicket has depreciated, it needs to if there’s going to be a result.
... DAY 5, SESSION 1 ...
A maiden for Holder! A bit of swing, on off. Alex Lees keeps it out.

Now a draw seems the most likeliest result. Unless we witness something special. England will probably hope to score some quick runs and then give themselves at least two sessions to have a crack at the Windies batting line-up. Windies on the other hand, will hope they can trigger a collapse in the first session. Do join us for what could be an interesting one. The action begins at 7.30 pm IST (2 pm GMT). But the build-up will begin in advance. Do join us for that. Until then, goodbye!

End of yet another dull day of cricket! The game needed to move on quickly if a result was needed but that was not the case. The Windies batted at their own pace and they batted for more than two sessions before being bundled out. England had around 15 overs to bat, they already had a lead of just under 100, they did play with a little intent but Root would have loved the two openers to go at a much better pace.

The umpires will be checking the light with the light metre. It has grown darker in the last few minutes. It is too dark for pace and Kraigg Brathwaite suggested to one of the umpires that they were going to bowl pace. So, the umpires have decided to call it STUMPS.
